text:
ben_support: Customer (acme-corp) reports sudden 401 with a hosted API key that had been working. They pasted the curl they run and the exact response. Key id: key_abc123. Error: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"Invalid API key."}

ben_support: Repro steps they gave:
```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer key_abc123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"hi"}'
```

carol_repro: I pulled the same request and see the 401 + these response headers: 

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
x-key-origin: dashboard
x-key-meta: sso_linked
x-key-state: deactivated
```

carol_repro: Quick note — the customer says the user who created the key was removed from their SSO (Okta) yesterday. They used the dashboard "Create API key" from their user profile, not the org service key flow.

dmitry_eng: :eyes: grabbing auth-service logs now. Can you confirm org id and full key id? Also please redact anything PII before sending to ENG.

ben_support: Org id: org_9876, key id: key_abc123 (redacted). Customer confirmed they removed the user during offboarding.

dmitry_eng: Found it in the logs:

```
auth-service.INFO revoke key_id=key_abc123 actor=system reason=SSO_user_deprovision timestamp=2024-06-04T15:02:12Z
telemetry: {deactivated_by_policy: "sso_deprovision", actor_id: "user:maria@acme-corp"}
```

dmitry_eng: That matches — keys created from a user profile are currently tagged as SSO-linked and are auto-deactivated when the linked SSO account is removed or deprovisioned. The API surface returns generic invalid_api_key which is confusing. I'll open a small change to make the error message clearer and emit x-deactivation-reason header. ETA: patch to beta tomorrow afternoon.

carol_repro: Workaround for customer: go to Org settings -> Service accounts -> Create service key. Service keys are not tied to a user and won't be auto-revoked on user deprovision. Confirmed a freshly created service key works for org_9876.

ben_support: Customer asked if we can re-activate key_abc123 instead of creating a service key.

dmitry_eng: We can re-activate manually but policy requires signed confirmation from an org admin because reactivation after deprovision is an audit-sensitive action. Please ask them to confirm in writing (admin email + reason). I'll create internal ticket ENG-5492 and flag security for audit review.

ben_support: Got it — I'll send instructions to the customer: 1) immediate workaround = create org service key (and rotate). 2) if they need the old key back, request admin confirmation and we'll review. I'll attach ENG-5492 when they respond. :lock:

support-bot: Label updated: escalated -> eng, SLA paused.

ben_support: Closing this thread for now pending customer reply. Will reopen if they request reactivation. :thumbsup:
